items.title: DOSH awaits full mitigation plan for fatal Paya Terubong landslide
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) is expected to receive the complete mitigation plan for the Taman Seri Rambai landslide in Paya Terubong tomorrow. State Local Government Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said Penang DOSH was awaiting the full submission and formal application from the developer's civil engineering firm, Aptitude Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd, which is acting as the project's superintending officer. "Penang DOSH's investigation and prosecution section had requested an incident report, and the developer's geotechnical engineer, WYA Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd, submitted it on Nov 5.

items.title: GOF lance corporal fined RM10,000 for possessing controlled poison
items.summary: LAHAD DATU: A General Operations Force (GOF) lance corporal was fined RM10,000 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to possessing 538ml of liquid containing Diphenhydramine, a controlled poison, in January. He was charged with possessing 538ml of liquid containing Diphenhydramine along Jalan Fajar at 12.30pm on Jan 31. A search of his bag and motorcycle basket uncovered 23 bottles of liquid suspected to be ketum water, with an estimated total volume of 34.5 litres, and six bottles of Dynadryl Syrup containing suspected cough medicine, with an estimated volume of 600ml.

items.title: Macron's Angkor visit highlights France's century-long conservation role
items.summary: SIEM REAP: The newly restored West Mebon temple rises from a reservoir at Cambodia's sprawling Angkor archaeological complex, the latest in a century of conservation projects led by former colonial power France. French President Emmanuel Macron and Cambodian King Norodom Sihamoni will inaugurate the nearly 1,000-year-old temple on the sidelines of a summit of French-speaking nations in Phnom Penh on Nov 15-16. The temple is part of the Unesco World Heritage site at Angkor, once the centre of the Khmer Empire, and includes the national treasure Angkor Wat.

items.title: KLCI to remain volatile amid US midterm election spillover [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The benchmark index FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI is expected to remain volatile amid geopolitical risks, domestic political uncertainties and inflationary pressures, as a global technology stock sell-off weighs on investor sentiment despite resilient domestic economic fundamentals. Affin Hwang Investment Bank head of research Loong Chee Wei expects the benchmark index to face continued volatility, with elevated global bond yields and uncertainty surrounding United States policies posing risks to financial markets. Technology stocks recorded the steepest declines among Bursa Malaysia's sectoral indices, reflecting concerns over potentially tighter US regulations on the AI industry.

items.title: Rapid KL foils second cable theft attempt in a week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An attempted theft of earthing cables along the MRT Putrajaya Line was foiled after a man was arrested in an intelligence-led operation by Rapid KL auxiliary police. Rapid KL said the arrest followed an attempted cable theft on Saturday, which disrupted train services on the line. Following the incident, auxiliary police and the Putrajaya Line operations team stepped up patrols, surveillance and security checks at identified high-risk locations, including during the Deepavali holiday period.

items.title: October building material costs – steel drops while sand inches up
items.summary: Monthly unit price index for sand rose between 0.3 and 1.8 per cent across selected areas, with Sandakan recording the highest monthly increase, followed by Kuching (0.8 per cent) and Johor (0.5 per cent). Cement price indices also recorded slight month-on-month gains ranging from 0.1 to 0.4 per cent. Perak posted the largest annual contraction at 8.2 per cent, followed by Terengganu and Kelantan (-4.8 per cent) and Miri (-4.0 per cent).

items.title: Sabah academic calls for transparency in infrastructure spending
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government should adopt a more transparent approach to infrastructure development, particularly in the disclosure of project details and public spending, said an academic. Universiti Teknologi Sabah senior lecturer Dr Jain Yassin said it was encouraging that the state government continued to prioritise basic infrastructure, particularly water supply and road connectivity. He said Sabah should begin investing in new sources of economic growth.

items.title: Oxford museum returns 39 Naga ancestral remains to India
items.summary: OXFORD: An Oxford University museum on Monday returned the remains of 39 people taken during Britain's colonial rule in India to members of its Naga community. The Oxford museum has more than 6,000 objects representing Naga culture, the largest collection in the world, and is giving back "ancestral human remains", mainly skulls, to the Naga people. The museum only removed all human remains from display in 2020, much later than most museums, and still has around 2,700 remains in storage, she told AFP.

items.title: Floods, storm and landslide leave 422 evacuees at relief centres in Perak, Selangor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — A total of 422 evacuees from 119 families remain at temporary relief centres (PPS) in Perak and Selangor as of this morning. In Perak, the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat said the number of flood evacuees had dropped to 410 people from 114 families, compared with 419 people from 124 families last night. It said all evacuees were currently housed at three PPS in two districts.

items.title: PH open to exploring new political cooperation after Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan will discuss its political direction, including the possibility of exploring new cooperation with other parties, only after the Melaka election. Acting Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said any decision on political cooperation must first be discussed by the PH Presidential Council before it could be regarded as the coalition's official position. Adam Adli said recent political developments did not necessarily reflect the parties' official positions unless the matters had been discussed and decided by the Presidential Council.

items.title: Malaysia's September IPI climbs 6.3pct as manufacturing sales hit RM191bil
items.summary: The manufacturing output sector advanced 9.4 per cent year-on-year (August 2026: 7.4 per cent), while electricity generation surged 10.7 per cent (August 2026: 9.0 per cent). On a month-on-month comparison, the IPI rose 1.3 per cent (August 2026: 2.6 per cent), supported by a 2.9 per cent expansion in the manufacturing sector. Domestic-oriented industries also gathered pace, rising 6.6 per cent year-on-year (August 2026: 3.9 per cent).

items.title: DAP committed to nation-building regardless of govt or opposition role, says veep Teo Nie Ching
items.summary: KULAI, Nov 10 — The DAP wants to continue playing its role as a nation-building party, regardless of whether it is in government or the opposition, by championing transparent, fair and sustainable policies, said its vice-president Teo Nie Ching. Teo, who is also deputy communications minister, said the principle formed the basis of DAP’s struggle to ensure Malaysia continued to develop as a nation with a sustainable governance system, while prioritising the interests and welfare of the people. Commenting on DAP’s participation in the Madani Government, Teo said its position provided the party with an opportunity to translate its principles into policies and action through direct involvement in the country’s administration.

items.title: Recently freed drug offender faces death penalty over heroin trafficking charge
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A man who was recently released after serving a sentence for a drug offence now faces the death penalty after being charged with trafficking 115g of heroin and possessing methamphetamine. The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act. The possession charge was framed under Section 12(2) of the Act and is punishable under Section 39A(1).

items.title: Three Myanmar children maintain innocence over intimidation charge, out on RM4,000 bail each
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Three Myanmar children pleaded not guilty at the magistrate's court today to a charge of criminally intimidating an elderly woman. The three — comprising two 11-year-olds and a 12-year-old — maintained their innocence after the joint charge was read to them in Myanmar by a court-appointed Myanmar interpreter before magistrate Roshayati Radellah. However, speaking to reporters after today's proceedings, Sagthiyaraj said all three children had since been released on RM4,000 bail each following an urgent revision at the High Court.

items.title: Too early for a Cabinet reshuffle, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said it was too early to discuss a Cabinet reshuffle amid speculation over possible changes to the line-up following Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s decision to resign. Utusan Malaysia reported today that the Cabinet could see changes involving two positions, namely the Transport Minister’s post following Loke’s resignation and the Second Finance Minister’s position held by Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan, whose three-year term as a senator is due to expire on December 11. The last Cabinet reshuffle took place on December 16 last year.

items.title: TM expands digital growth across AI, cloud and cybersecurity
items.summary: TELEKOM Malaysia (TM) is expanding its capabilities in artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, cybersecurity and digital infrastructure as it seeks to translate its technological strengths into stronger business growth. TM's success in securing awards across four categories at the PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards 2026 reflects its ongoing transformation and growing focus on digital services. At the core of TM's strategy is a scalable, end-to-end digital ecosystem designed to reduce operational friction and accelerate growth for consumers and businesses.

items.title: Melaka polls: EC targets 95pc early voter turnout as 53.25pc cast ballots by 10.35am
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 10 — The Election Commission (EC) is targeting a voter turnout of up to 95 per cent for the early voting phase of the 16th Melaka state election today. “Today, 9,769 military personnel and 2,762 police personnel are participating in the early voting process, bringing the total number of early voters to 12,531,” he said. The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as the polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting is taking place today.

items.title: EC targets 95 per cent turnout for Melaka early voting
items.summary: MELAKA: The Election Commission is targeting a 95 per cent turnout for early voting in the Melaka election today. He said a total of 9,769 military personnel and 2,792 police personnel were eligible to vote in the early voting today. "Early voting has begun at 31 polling centres across Melaka, involving 50 streams.

items.title: Malaysia aims to build one million affordable homes by 2035 using advanced construction technology, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Malaysia aims to deliver 500,000 affordable homes by 2030 and one million by 2035 through the adoption and development of advanced modular construction technology, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. He said technology must help the country build homes more efficiently and affordably without compromising safety, quality and liveability. “Now technology must help us deliver these homes more efficiently, without compromising forsafety, quality and liveability,” he said when officiating the International Construction Week and BuildXPO Malaysia 2026 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec) here.

items.title: Growing data centre demand for electricity an opportunity for Petronas – Johari
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) could tap new opportunities in the domestic natural gas market as Malaysia's growing data centre industry drives demand for electricity, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He said the rising electricity requirements of data centres could create another commercially attractive market for natural gas, provided it is supplied at market prices without subsidies. However, with the growth of data centres, there is an opportunity to supply gas for power generation and sell electricity at retail prices.

items.title: EC, MCMC take measures to protect website following reported cyber attack
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 10 — The Election Commission (EC) is working with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and other relevant parties to strengthen the security of its website following reports of a suspected cyber attack. EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said a report on the incident had also been submitted to the relevant authorities as an initial measure to ensure the commission’s systems remain protected. Ramlan said the EC would also issue an official statement on the matter soon.

items.title: Four more bodies recovered in Pertak water surge tragedy, three missing
items.summary: HULU SELANGOR: Four bodies of victims swept away by a water surge at Lata Jebus, Sungai Luit, Kampung Pertak, were retrieved from the river at 11.15am today, while three others remain missing. A check at the scene found three bodies trapped along the riverbank near Jambatan Senget, about 950m from Lata Jebus, at 9.20am. Earlier, a 36-year-old local man was found dead near Pertak Bridge at 1.30am today.

items.title: Two Chinese tourists among three injured in boat collision off Semporna
items.summary: SEMPORNA: Three people, including two Chinese tourists, were injured after their tourist boat suffered engine trouble and was rammed by another vessel near Pulau Singamata yesterday. The incident occurred at 11.12am as the boat, carrying eight Chinese tourists, a skipper and three crew members, was travelling from Seafest Jetty to Pulau Bohey Dulang. The first boat sustained damage to its rear section, while the skipper and a crew member of the second boat escaped unhurt.

items.title: Too early to discuss cabinet reshuffle, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said it was too early to discuss the possibility of a cabinet reshuffle. This follows speculation over the positions of Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan and Transport Minister Anthony Loke, amid the possibility of two vacancies in the cabinet. "It's too early," Anwar said when asked about a cabinet reshuffle.

items.title: Floods forecast in Rompin, Jerantut from tomorrow until Nov 14
items.summary: "In Rompin, areas at risk include low-lying locations within a 5km radius of the Rompin River Basin, covering Kampung Aur, Kampung Meripoh, Kampung Tebu Hitam, Pantai Bernas, Kampung Ayau, Leban Chondong, Kampung Gading and Kampung Sarang Tiong. "Other areas include low-lying locations within a 5km radius of the Pahang River Basin, covering Kampung Mikang, Kampung Buluh Nipis, Kampung Simpang Sepayang, Kampung Sepayang, Kampung Tebu Hitam, Kampung Tengah, Kampung Tekek, Perumahan Murah Kampung Tekek, Kampung Serinkin, and Kampung Janglau 1, 2 and 3," it said. Other locations include Kampung Baharu, Kampung Besul, Kampung Jerangsang, Kampung Sungai Siam, Kampung Lata Kasah, Kampung Kuala Pengau, Kampung Kuala Teh, Kampung Batu Balai, Kampung Sempadan, Felda Sungai Retang, Felda Padang Piol and Kampung Paya Garuk.

items.title: Melaka polls: Police receive 19 reports, open 18 investigation papers, make no arrests
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 10 — Melaka police have received 19 reports involving various offences, including mischief, mischief by fire and fighting, since campaigning for the 16th Melaka state election began on October 31. Dzulkhairi said 669 police personnel had been deployed across the state to monitor election campaigning and maintain public safety and order. On preparations for polling day this Saturday, he said 3,332 police personnel would be deployed, including officers assigned to monitor the voting process at polling centres throughout the state.

items.title: Police probe fireworks display at Jalan Kuala Kangsar junction
items.summary: IPOH: Police are investigating a fireworks display at a traffic junction along Jalan Kuala Kangsar after a video of the incident went viral on Threads. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said police had yet to receive any reports on the incident. However, he said police would investigate the incident to identify those involved and establish the circumstances surrounding it.

items.title: Singaporean lured by RM12,685 job offer arrested, remanded seven days over RM1.5m cannabis haul at Ipoh Airport
items.summary: Perak police chief Commissioner Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspect had been tricked by a syndicate into believing he was transporting a package containing counterfeit luxury-branded goods. He said that the syndicate was believed to have targeted less busy airports, concealing drugs in passengers’ luggage to avoid detection by the authorities. Mohd Alwi said the amount of drugs seized could have been used by about 47,900 addicts.

items.title: Foreign institution continues buying Malaysian stocks
items.summary: Tuesday recorded the highest net foreign inflow at RM152.4 million, followed by Monday at RM102.5 million. This was followed by Thursday with RM55 million, Friday with RM40.6 million and Wednesday with RM30.8 million. "The top three sectors with net inflows from foreign institutions were financial services (RM249.5 million), transportation and logistics (RM199.8 million) and construction (RM191.4 million).

items.title: China's trade surplus soars past US$1tril as AI boom powers exports
items.summary: BEIJING: China's trade surplus surged past US$1 trillion in the first 10 months as a global race to build AI infrastructure buoyed sales of high-tech products and helped offset weak domestic demand, a dynamic likely to sharpen tensions with major trading partners. That helped lift China's trade surplus to US$1.04 trillion in the first 10 months, topping US$1 trillion for a second consecutive year and reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025. SEO keywords: China trade surplus, China's exports, AI infrastructure, China trade tensions, global trade demand © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Melaka polls: EC awaiting full report on website cyberattack
items.summary: MELAKA: The Election Commission is investigating claims that its website was targeted in a cyberattack during the Melaka election. Its chairman, Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun, said the commission had yet to receive a full report on the matter and would issue a statement soon. God willing," he said.

items.title: Switch to defensive stocks as investors move away from manufacturers, tech, says BIMB
items.summary: It said the investment strategy had shifted towards defensive sectors, particularly banking and domestic infrastructure, as institutional investors moved away from export-oriented manufacturers and technology stocks. The sell-off also spread across Asian markets, with Taiwan's TWSE, South Korea's KOSPI and Japan's Nikkei falling 12.2 per cent, 11.7 per cent and 9.3 per cent respectively last week, reflecting their exposure to the global AI hardware supply chain. The FBM KLCI closed at 1,616 points, up 0.31 per cent week-on-week last week, but remained down 3.78 per cent year-to-date.

items.title: Melaka polls: Former assemblyman rallies behind Tuminah in Pantai Kundor
items.summary: MELAKA: Former Pantai Kundor assemblyman Datuk Nor Azman Hassan is putting past political differences aside to help Barisan Nasional candidate Datuk Tuminah Kadi defend the seat in the Melaka election. Nor Azman, who won the seat for BN in the 2018 General Election, lost to Tuminah in the 2021 Melaka election when he contested as a Pakatan Harapan candidate. Tuminah, who represented Umno, defeated Nor Azman by a majority of 827 votes.

items.title: S$4k offer lands Singaporean in RM1.5mil cannabis bust
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspect was detained at Sultan Azlan Shah Airport (LTSAS) here at 6.20am on Sunday. He said auxiliary police personnel spotted the suspicious luggage during a routine inspection at the airport's check-in counter. Alwi said the drugs weighed 19.04kg and were estimated to be worth RM1.52 million.

items.title: Water surge at Pertak river: Four more bodies found, bringing toll to five
items.summary: HULU SELANGOR, Nov 10 — Four more bodies of victims swept away by strong currents at Sungai Pertak in Kuala Kubu Bharu were found this morning, bringing the number of victims located to five out of the eight reported missing. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said three victims were found trapped near Jambatan Senget, close to the Sungai Luit campsite, at 9.20am, Utusan Malaysia reported. The incident occurred at about 5.55pm yesterday, when eight people — comprising one Yemeni national, one Malaysian, one Sri Lankan, one Nepalese and four Indian nationals — were swept away by the current.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 10, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index opened higher, following Wall Street's rally on Monday as lower oil prices eased inflation concerns. The key index gained nearly 10 points to 1,626.55. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin rebounded to RM305,874.

items.title: Najib house arrest: Home minister says court must clarify Prisons Dept’s authority
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 10 — The interpretation of the Conditional Pardon Order and the implications of the Order of Discharge involving Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak require further clarification to establish whether the Prisons Department has the authority to implement house arrest for the former prime minister. The Order of Discharge states that he is to be released, whereas the Pardons Board refers to house arrest. House arrest is different from release.

items.title: GOF seizes 1.2 tonnes of suspected smuggled rice in Tumpat
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 1,216kg of various brands of rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand during a raid in Kampung Kubang Panjang, Tumpat, yesterday. The rice, valued at RM4,864, was seized during Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan around 4pm after members of Strike Force Company B, Battalion 7 of the Kuantan GOF, spotted a suspicious Nissan Vanette van while patrolling the Kota Baru-Pengkalan Kubor route. Radzi said the case had been referred to the Kelantan Padi and Rice Regulatory Department for further action under Section 20 of the National Padi and Rice Regulatory Act.

items.title: GOF seizes 1.2 tonnes of suspected Thai smuggled rice in Tumpat
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 10 — The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 1,216 kilogrammes of various brands of rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand during a raid in Kampung Kubang Panjang, Tumpat, yesterday. The seizure, valued at RM4,864, was made during Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan at about 4pm after members of Strike Force Company B, Battalion 7 of the Kuantan GOF, spotted a suspicious Nissan Vanette van while patrolling the Kota Bharu-Pengkalan Kubor route. An inspection of the van uncovered 49 sacks of rice of various brands, comprising 750 kg bearing the Mangga label, 250 kg with the Nangka label, 120 kg with the Serindit label, 72 kg with the Angsa Mas label and 24 kg with the Pisang label.

items.title: [UPDATED] Sungai Pertak water surge: Four more victims found dead
items.summary: Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said three victims were found trapped near Jambatan Senget, close to the Sungai Luit campsite around 9.20am. Earlier, a 36-year-old local man was found dead near Jambatan Pertak around 1.30am today. "Sector C covers the Jambatan Dam area, while Sector D covers the dam area," he said.

items.title: Trump signals progress towards ending Iran war after Qatar PM meeting
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday there was "positive momentum" toward ending the war with Iran after meeting Qatar's prime minister at the White House. "I had an excellent conversation with Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani," Trump said on Truth Social, adding that "much was discussed with respect to the Islamic Republic of Iran." In the weeks leading up to the vote, there was widespread speculation that US strikes against Iran would resume soon after.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan’s Jegasilan wants to create jobs in Gadek through modern farming
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Nov 10 — Gadek has the potential to become a hub for modern agriculture and livestock farming, creating job opportunities for local youths and reducing their need to seek employment elsewhere, particularly in Singapore. Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Gadek state seat, Jegasilan K, 45, said the area still had vast tracts of land that could be developed for modern vegetable cultivation and livestock farming. He said former rubber plantations could be transformed into agricultural areas producing various crops for local markets, alongside livestock hubs for poultry and cattle.

items.title: MOE gets 670 school maintenance applications in first week of special channel, says Fadhlina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has received 670 applications from Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs) nationwide for school maintenance allocations, just a week after the launch of the MOE PTA special channel on November 1. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, in a Facebook post today, said the strong response reflected PTAs’ commitment to working together with the ministry to improve school facilities and create a more conducive environment for students. It shows the determination of PTAs to work together to help improve school facilities and environments for the comfort of our children,” she said.

items.title: Penang water operator boosts security after vandalism, theft at Pokok Sena canal
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Nov 10 — The Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) has tightened security and stepped up patrols along the Pokok Sena Canal here following incidents of trespassing, vandalism and theft. In a statement today, PBAPP said the incidents came to light during a routine security patrol by its auxiliary police, with subsequent checks revealing that several infrastructure components in the canal area had been damaged or were missing. PBAPP subsequently lodged a police report at 1.07pm yesterday to facilitate further investigations into the incidents.

items.title: North-east monsoon: Kelantan Fire Dept readies 35 boats for flood rescues
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 10 — A total of 35 of the 45 boats belonging to the Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) are operational and ready for deployment during the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon, said its director Farhan Sufyan Borhan. Farhan Sufyan said boats were among the most critical assets in flood rescue operations, particularly in flooded areas inaccessible to land vehicles. The department currently has eight three- and five-tonne lorries and 30 four-wheel-drive vehicles stationed at 22 fire stations across Kelantan, he said.

items.title: Melaka polls: Early voting begins smoothly as security personnel turn out
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 10 — The early voting process for the 16th Melaka state election proceeded smoothly this morning, with many security personnel taking advantage of the clear weather early in the day to arrive at the polling centres. At the polling centre located in the multipurpose hall of the Melaka police contingent headquarters (IPK), a Bernama observation noted that eligible police personnel began arriving as early as 7.30am, lining up to cast their votes starting at 7.53am. A total of 817 police personnel are set to cast their early votes at this location.

items.title: Two burnt to death, two injured as Mercedes catches fire after crash in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 10 — Two people were burnt to death while two others were injured after a car they were travelling in caught fire, following an accident near the Permas Jaya Golf Club, along the road heading towards Bakar Batu, early today. Johor Jaya Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) Operations Commander PBK I Razali Hussein said the department received an emergency call about the incident at about 4.35am. Two of them were found burnt inside the vehicle, while three others managed to escape from the vehicle before firefighters arrived,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan’s Ginie Lim uses interactive digital platform to reach Machap Jaya voters
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 10 — The Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for Machap Jaya state constituency, Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin, is leveraging on an interactive digital platform to reach out to voters for the Melaka state election and to enhance their understanding of the electoral process. Through the website https://ginielim.com/, voters can access a wealth of information about the candidate including her biography, background, manifesto, and campaign tour schedule while also engaging through various provided communication channels. Lim noted that the platform features an interactive game that challenges users to reach 8,015 clicks within 90 seconds, encouraging participation, alongside a simulation game designed to demonstrate the correct voting procedure.

items.title: Factory worker killed after motorcycle crashes into Proton that veered into his path in Kluang
items.summary: KLUANG, Nov 10 — A factory worker was killed yesterday after his Yamaha motorcycle crashed into a car that had veered into his path along Jalan Anggerik near Felda Kahang Barat. Kluang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said the victim was travelling from Gunung Berlumut towards Jalan Padang Tembak when the accident occurred. At the same time, a Proton car driven by a 29-year-old man was travelling in the opposite direction, while a Toyota driven by a 45-year-old man with two passengers was behind the victim.

items.title: Gardenia East Malaysia issues corporate clarification amid food poisoning case
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 10 — Gardenia Bakeries (East Malaysia) Sdn Bhd has clarified that it is a separate business entity from Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd, following complaints of alleged food poisoning involving Gardenia products that have attracted public attention on social media. “Gardenia Bakeries (East Malaysia) Sdn Bhd and Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd are two separate business entities with different ownership and management structures,” he said in a statement on Sunday. Lau’s clarification comes amid a Ministry of Health (MoH) investigation into complaints of alleged food poisoning after consuming Gardenia Original Classic White Bread and Twiggies Choc-A-Lot.

items.title: Sarawak to keep pushing for greater rights under MA63, says Abang Johari
items.summary: SEBAUH, Nov 10 — Sarawak will continue defending its rights under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), said caretaker Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg. Abang Johari said the state’s position was strengthened by unity among its people and the state’s political leadership. Also present were caretaker Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas; Sarawak Legislative Assembly Speaker Tan Sri Datuk Amar Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar; Malaysia Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing; caretaker Minister for Food Industry, Commodity and Regional Development Dato Sri Dr Stephen Rundi Utom; Sarawak State Secretary Datuk Amar Mohamad Abu Bakar Marzuki; and Bintulu Resident Datu Nyurak Keti.

items.title: Cyber threats to Malaysia now extend beyond data theft to daily disruption, Nacsa says
items.summary: National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) Chief Executive Dr Megat Zuhairy Megat Tajuddin said Malaysia was not exempt from this threat, particularly attacks targeting industrial control systems in the healthcare, energy, water supply and supply chain sectors. From a legal perspective, Megat Zuhairy stressed that the Cyber Security Act 2024 (Act 854) required NCII entities to comply with stringent security practices to ensure the resilience of their respective service systems. For organisations that are not classified as NCII entities, Nacsa has issued the Cyber Security Threat Preparedness and Handling Guidelines as a reference to enhance preparedness, early detection, threat response and service continuity.

items.title: Flood warning issued for low-lying areas in Jerantut, Rompin in Pahang from tomorrow
items.summary: “Other affected areas include Kampung Sungai Siam, Kampung Lata Kasah, Kampung Kuala Pengau, Kampung Kuala Teh, Kampung Batu Balai, Kampung Sempadan, Felda Sungai Retang, Felda Padang Piol and Kampung Paya Garuk,” the statement said. Meanwhile, in Rompin, the warning covers low-lying areas within a five-kilometre radius of the Sungai Rompin river basin, including Kampung Aur, Kampung Meripoh, Kampung Tebu Hitam, Pantai Bernas, Kampung Ayau, Leban Chondong, Kampung Gading and Kampung Sarang Tiong. The warning also extends to low-lying areas within a five-kilometre radius of the Sungai Pahang river basin, including Kampung Mikang, Kampung Buluh Nipis, Kampung Simpang Sepayang, Kampung Sepayang, Kampung Tebu Hitam, Kampung Tengah, Kampung Tekek, the Kampung Tekek low-cost housing area, Kampung Serinkin and Kampung Janglau 1, 2 and 3.

items.title: Pertak river surge: One body recovered, seven still missing in Kuala Kubu Bharu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — One of the eight individuals reported missing following a water surge at Sungai Pertak, Kuala Kubu Bharu, near here yesterday, was found drowned near the Pertak Bridge this morning. Earlier, media reports indicated that during an incident at approximately 5.55pm yesterday, eight people consisting of one Yemeni national, one local, one Sri Lankan, one Nepalese, and four Indian nationals went missing after being swept away by the current. He added that the search and rescue (SAR) operation resumed this morning, with the search area divided into four sectors around the incident site to locate the seven remaining missing individuals.

items.title: Anwar says SoftBank-led AI investment signals global confidence in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The SoftBank-led consortium’s investment in an artificial intelligence (AI) platform in Malaysia reflects global confidence in the country’s potential to develop and use AI, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. SoftBank chief executive officer Masayoshi Son reportedly selected Kuching, Sarawak, and Peninsular Malaysia for US$50 billion (RM202.86 billion) in AI infrastructure investments. According to Anwar, combining SoftBank’s capital and expertise with Grab’s regional AI capabilities and proven track record of deploying AI across its ecosystem would significantly enhance Malaysia’s AI infrastructure and global competitiveness.

items.title: Pertak river surge leaves eight missing, nine stranded in Kuala Kubu Bharu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Eight people remain missing after they were swept away by swift currents, while nine others are reported to be stranded in three separate incidents involving different groups when the water level of Sungai Pertak surged in Kuala Kubu Bharu near here yesterday evening. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department asst operations director Asrul Riezal Asbar the eight missing included an individual from a group of Yemeni nationals and locals, and seven from a group of 11 locals. The nine stranded individuals included four that did not cross the river and five from another group reported to be stranded across the river.

items.title: Melaka polls: 31 early voting centres open at 8am
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 10 — Thirty-one early polling centres for the 16th Melaka State Election opened at 8am today to allow 12,531 security personnel and their spouses to cast their ballots. The election sees Pakatan Harapan fielding candidates in 24 state seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (23), Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five), Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (one), and three Independents. In the 2021 Melaka State Election, Barisan Nasional won 21 seats to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan won five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.

items.title: Instant torque, heavier batteries: What Malaysian motorists need to know before driving an EV
items.summary: “Instant torque does not make every EV fast or hard to control, as performance depends on motor output, vehicle weight, gearing, traction, and drive mode. Acceleration is shaped by tyre grip, vehicle mass, and driver input, not torque alone,” he said. Why does an EV accelerate differently from an ICE vehicle?

items.title: Malaysians still feel prices are high despite easing inflation, Bank Negara explains why
items.summary: This may be why Malaysians still feel financially stretched even when official inflation figures indicate that price increases are slowing. Inflation averaged 1.8 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, with core inflation at 2 per cent. By emphasising these regular purchases, BNM said the EPI captures price changes that more closely mirror households’ day-to-day experiences.

items.title: Can Malaysia turn monsoon floods into drought-proof water reserves instead?
items.summary: Therefore, the main challenge now is to what extent some of the water overflow during the North-east Monsoon (MTL) can be harvested, stored, and reused optimally during hot weather to reduce pressure on the water supply system and the agricultural sector. Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP) water resource expert Associate Professor Dr Zulkarnain Hassan said Malaysia needs to emphasise efforts to maximise rainwater harvesting, especially in areas receiving heavy rainfall such as the East Coast of Peninsular Malaysia, as well as Sabah and Sarawak. Touching on dam management, Zulkarnain said the main challenge is optimising the operation of multi-purpose dams, particularly in balancing the need to release water to reduce flood risk without compromising the dry season storage reserves.
